title: Women's T20 World Cup Gets New Schedule as ICC Moves India-Pakistan Clash to Dubai
excerpt: The ICC has unveiled a revised itinerary for the Women's T20 World Cup, relocating the tournament from Bangladesh to the UAE and scheduling the marquee India-Pakistan contest for October 6 in Dubai.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The Women's T20 World Cup is relocated to the UAE from Bangladesh due to political instability.
  • India will play Pakistan in Dubai on October 6, with the final on October 20.
  • Group compositions remain unchanged, featuring teams like Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa.
  • The tournament runs from October 3 to 20, with reserve days for semifinals and final.
  • UAE's large South Asian population enhances accessibility for fans attending the matches.
  • The ICC has moved the Women's T20 World Cup from Bangladesh to the UAE, with matches split between Dubai and Sharjah from October 3-20.
  • India will face Pakistan in Dubai on October 6, with the final also scheduled at the same venue on October 20.
  • The relocation was driven by political instability in Bangladesh, and the revised schedule keeps the original group compositions intact.
  • If India qualify for the knockout stage, they will play their semifinal in Dubai on October 17.

Tournament Relocates to UAE

The International Cricket Council has unveiled a revised schedule for the Women's T20 World Cup, moving the entire tournament from Bangladesh to the United Arab Emirates after the ongoing political crisis in Dhaka made hosting untenable. Dubai and Sharjah will now share duties for the 18-day competition running from October 3 to 20, according to Cricbuzz.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DabSoS5Eru2/

The restructured itinerary places the biggest draw of the tournament — India versus Pakistan — in Dubai on October 6, a Sunday afternoon slot designed to maximise viewership. Dubai will also host the final on October 20, giving the venue the tournament's two most high-profile fixtures.

Group Stage and Schedule Details

The groups remain unchanged from the original draw. Group A features six-time champions Australia alongside India, New Zealand, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Group B comprises South Africa, England, West Indies, Bangladesh and Scotland. Each team plays four group matches, with the top two from each group advancing to the semifinals.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=NeBMvO6xAkc

India's campaign opens against New Zealand in Dubai on October 4, followed by the Pakistan clash two days later. Harmanpreet Kaur's side then face Sri Lanka in Dubai on October 9 before travelling to Sharjah for their final group match against Australia on October 13 — the only fixture India will play outside Dubai.

"The ICC has ensured that the tournament maintains its competitive integrity while providing a safe and world-class hosting environment for all participating teams."

— ICC Statement on the Women's T20 World Cup relocation

What It Means for Fans

The move to the UAE significantly changes the accessibility equation for fans. The Gulf's large South Asian expatriate population — estimated at over eight million Indians alone — makes this a natural market for cricket events. Both Dubai and Sharjah have hosted major ICC events before, including the 2021 Men's T20 World Cup.

Teams Advancing to Semifinals

Reserve days have been fixed for both semifinals and the final, reducing the risk of weather-related disruptions. Ten warm-up matches are scheduled from September 28 through October 1.

India's Preparations

India head into the tournament with mixed recent form. Losses to South Africa and England in the lead-up have exposed vulnerabilities, particularly around the middle-order composition following the return of injury-recovered Yastika Bhatia. The trial period has delivered uneven results and diluted lower-order hitting depth.

For Pakistan, captain Fatima Sana's fitness remains a concern after she suffered a right knee injury during practice. Her availability for the India match is uncertain, and fellow senior player Aliya Riaz was also absent from recent training sessions.

Looking Ahead

The Women's T20 World Cup arrives at a pivotal moment for women's cricket globally. The India-Pakistan rivalry, regardless of the relative gap between the two sides on paper, consistently delivers the tournament's most-watched contests. Pakistan have given India several scares beyond their two World Cup victories, and captain Fatima Sana's aggressive approach — if she is fit — could produce another compelling chapter in the rivalry.
